blocking_findings.summary: ASKFLOOR-1-T5b-AC2: LISTING. Bare `/permissions` in a DM renders today's mode line, then the ten newest ACTIVE current-rails records as "<Outcome> · <scope noun> · <place> · <d Mon> · <label>" (+ " · used by job <a>, <b>" or "+N jobs" per ruling 4) each with a `memory_forget { recordId, agentRouteKey, label: 'Forget <shortId>' }` affordance, then the footer lines when more exist; the empty state when none; `/permissions all` renders every active record as plain text with the short id first; dates use the configured timezone, day + month. NEW `application/permissions/permission-memory-listing.ts` owns every row and reply string and the `PermissionMemoryListMessageView`; nouns come from the existing application helpers (category noun / "<tool label>, this exact call"). Tests: NEW listing suite — row format from real T3-shaped rows (scopeKey-decoded category and place, `canonicalRoot` null, the literal Bash exact-call example) incl. "someone" fallback, exact "2 Sep" under a foreign process locale, timezone day-crossing date, agentRouteKey round-trip / max-size / unknown / collision, ten-newest cut + footer, empty state, `all` ordering (newest first) and short-id-first, used-by suffix with 1, 2, 3+ jobs, a deleted job omitted before the +N count, one job used twice rendered once.

ASKFLOOR-1-T5b-AC5: USED-BY READ. `listDecisionsByHumanDecisionRecordId` on the port + Postgres adapter: one row per `(recordId, jobId)`, latest use, ordered `lastUsedAt DESC, jobId`, filtered by app and record ids, extracted from `actor_context_json`; no index (owner-accepted scan, recorded as an assumption at pr-ready). The used-by reader hydrates names via `getJobById`, drops deleted jobs first, names two, then "+N jobs". Tests: Postgres integration (rows written through `recordDecision` with `humanDecisionRecordId` on both job lanes are returned once per job with the latest timestamp; unrelated rows and other apps are not), reader unit (1, 2, 3+ jobs; deleted job dropped before the count; ordering).

non_blocking_findings.summary: [P2] Keep the list-view type in the required application owner (apps/core/src/domain/message-actions.ts:3): The contract explicitly makes `application/permissions/permission-memory-listing.ts` the owner of `PermissionMemoryListMessageView`, but the patch defines that interface in `domain/message-actions.ts` and imports it into the listing module.

[P2] Reuse the authoritative category-noun formatter (apps/core/src/application/permissions/permission-memory-listing.ts:160): The listing module introduces its own `CATEGORY_NOUNS` mapping even though AC2 and the load-bearing constitution require these nouns to come from the existing application helpers.

[P2] Add the required one- and two-job used-by cases (apps/core/test/unit/application/permission-memory-listing.test.ts:215): The new listing suite exercises only the 3+ jobs path (including deletion and duplicate-use handling).

contract_verdicts.evidence: apps/core/src/session/session-command-parse.ts:29 implements the two new parser forms.

apps/core/src/domain/message-actions.ts:3 places the required application-owned view outside its owner, and apps/core/src/application/permissions/permission-memory-listing.ts:160 duplicates the noun mapping.
apps/core/src/app/bootstrap/permission-memory-forget-handler.ts:27 implements the person-, route-, and rails-scoped button path.

apps/core/src/channels/telegram/callback-handlers.ts:489, apps/core/src/channels/slack/channel-message-action-handler.ts:110, and apps/core/src/channels/teams/message-actions.ts:292 implement the provider outcomes.
apps/core/test/unit/application/permission-memory-listing.test.ts:215 covers only the 3+ used-by case, omitting the required one- and two-job cases.
apps/core/src/runtime/group-processing.ts:156 and apps/core/src/runtime/ipc-interaction-processing.ts:211 carry the host-derived label and group identity behavior.

apps/core/src/application/agents/prompt-profile-service.ts:218 and apps/core/test/unit/runtime/askfloor-tap-budget.test.ts:123 provide the guidance and S5 evidence; the recorded verification gates pass.
